description: Schedule one-time executable work after a delay. Configure exactly one execution mode: provide a non-empty action_definitions list of syntactically valid {process_key, arguments} objects, or provide memory_tag for the terminal get_memories_by_tag read. Registration validates entry shape and scheduled-action policy; execution resolves process_key against processes registered at fire time. Content is valid only with memory_tag and is stored only after the complete request validates; the later lookup result is written to the schedule result row and does not start a model turn. Use direct action definitions for deterministic notifications, mechanizable Joseki runs, timeouts, polling actions, and other mechanizable work. Cancel via clear_scheduled_actions_by_tag. Registered plugin and service calls return a queued job receipt (job_id, status). Read service_interface::job_service::get_job with that exact id until terminal; the complete operation envelope is in job.result and a typed failure is in job.error. Admission alone does not confirm registration, recovery or history completion. The owner worker includes argument preparation, optional embedding, memory-history scans and recovery activation/CAS work; direct internal Python calls retain final results. A lost volatile request or an uncertain effect requires reconciliation, never automatic replay.
embedding_description: Schedule one-time executable work in N seconds. action_definitions requires non-empty, syntactically valid {process_key, arguments} entries; execution resolves each process_key against processes registered at fire time. memory_tag is the mutually exclusive terminal mode: it performs get_memories_by_tag, records the result, and does not start a model turn. Content is valid only with memory_tag. Cancel via clear_scheduled_actions_by_tag.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Queued job receipt with job_id and status; the terminal job.result contains the complete operation envelope. Confirmation of one-time delayed execution with schedule_id, delay time, and run_at timestamp
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Retain job_id and poll the exact job via job_service::get_job. Continue only after completed, or handle the typed job.error. A delayed execution schedule has been created. Consider whether you should inform the requester when the check-in/reminder will occur, and retain the schedule_id or tags so it can be cancelled or replaced once underlying work completes.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Scheduling one-time delayed execution with direct action definitions or a terminal memory lookup
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: default_scheduling_plugin.parameter_error: non-positive seconds, malformed or inference-bearing action definition, empty action list, invalid memory_tag, content outside memory_tag mode, or an execution-mode conflict. default_scheduling_plugin.schedule_create_error: persistence or scheduler registration failed after valid parameters.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For seconds errors: provide a positive integer for the delay. For execution-mode errors: use non-empty {process_key, arguments} action definitions for executable work, or a non-empty memory_tag only when a terminal tagged-memory read is the complete intent. For scheduler errors: verify the scheduling service is running.
